newsitem.title: USA: Brent dips in late US trade, foreign crudes steady.
newsitem.headline: Brent dips in late US trade, foreign crudes steady.

text.p: Benchmark North Sea Brent dropped in late U.S. trading Friday in a continuing trend linked to heavy selling by a top Wall Street firm, traders said.
A series of partial paper March Brent cargoes changed hands at $22.40/22.45/22.47/22.48 and 22.52 twice, down up to 13 cents from the IPE settlement.
Intermonth spreads were also weaker. February/March Brent spreads traded twice at 24 cents and once at 25 cents a barrel, down from 41 cents at the London close.
In physical trade, the flow of foreign crudes into the U.S. Gulf Coast was steady although demand is still lackluster, trader said.
Transatlantic trade continues apace, fueled by the wide arbitrage between benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent. March WTI/Brent was around $1.85-90 a barrel.
A U.S. company is showing Brent for early March at March WTI minus 40 cents, traders said.
A leading broker was heard to have sold West African Cabinda, loading January 27-29, to two Gulf Coast refiners at an undisclosed price, traders said.
Latin American spot activity was subdued. Latin sweet grades, such as Cusiana, have dropped in recent weeks in response to the barrage of North Sea and west African brudes on the Gulf Coast.
